audit_findings.title: The historical OE series contains catastrophic unit errors
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2018 $58,805.9m and FY2019 $65,638.0m, approximately 1,000 times the surrounding OE observations
audit_findings.mechanism: Corrupted historical OE enters the log-trend calculation that produced the $63.5m anchor and also caused the too-hard fallback.
audit_findings.evidence: The following tables provide our key business metrics for our consolidated entity (in thousands, except per share amounts):
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated data error, not merely a possibility. The two observations are incompatible with the filing's stated thousands-based units and the company's financial scale. Because the selected anchor depends on the corrupted trend, the operating valuation cannot be relied upon. The correction's direction cannot be established until the trend is rerun.
audit_findings.action: Re-extract every OE component with explicit source units, correct FY2018 and FY2019, validate all years for the same conversion error, and rerun anchor selection and every scenario.

audit_findings.title: The perimeter cannot be null after the strategic financing-business divestiture
audit_findings.magnitude: Sale proceeds $164.2m; discontinued-operations net earnings $8.516m in FY2026, $28.137m in FY2025, and $20.655m in FY2024; exact valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Pre-divestiture financing earnings or reinvestment may enter historical OE while sale proceeds remain within the $448.854m cash bridge, creating an inconsistent trend and possible double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: This divestiture positions us to focus on being a technology solutions provider and represents a strategic shift in our operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that FY2024-FY2026 comparative income statements were retrospectively recast, but it does not establish that the valuation's older FY2017-FY2023 OE observations use the same continuing-operations perimeter. The discontinued earnings are large relative to the $63.5m anchor, and sale proceeds equal 25.9% of the $633.5m total represented by anchor OE plus bridge cash, so unresolved perimeter contamination is reasonably capable of changing value materially.
audit_findings.action: Map every OE year to continuing operations, remove sold domestic-financing results and associated noncash and reinvestment items where present, identify retained international-financing results, reconcile the $164.2m proceeds within cash, and rerun the anchor and bridge.

audit_findings.title: Owner earnings appear to omit material working-capital reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 continuing-operations operating cash flow was negative $117.447m versus stated OE of $139.1m; FY2025 operating cash flow was positive $323.918m; normalized working-capital charge unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An omitted normalized working-capital investment inflates OE and makes projected growth appear distributable without funding the associated receivables, inventory, deferred costs, and payable cycle.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended March 31, 2026, we used $117.4 million through operating activities of continuing operations primarily due to increases in accounts receivable and inventory and decreases in accounts payable, partially offset by net earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a working-capital-driven FY2026 cash shortfall whose absolute amount is 84.4% of stated FY2026 OE and 185.0% of anchor OE. The opposite FY2025 cash movement shows that the full annual outflow cannot simply be treated as recurring, but it does not justify a zero charge. A cycle-normalized requirement is therefore both unresolved and reasonably capable of materially reducing operating value.
audit_findings.action: Calculate multi-year incremental working capital using trade receivables, inventory, deferred costs, trade and floor-plan payables, contract liabilities, and revenue or gross-billings growth; separate timing reversals from structural investment and rerun OE and growth scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The bridge treats all cash as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $448.854m, equal to $17.08 per diluted share and 33.5% of the $1,341m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for operations, working capital, customer obligations, taxes, acquisitions, or restricted entities must be excluded from the excess-cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We use those funds to meet our capital requirements, which primarily consist of working capital for operational needs, capital expenditures, mergers and acquisitions, the issuance of dividends and repurchase of shares of our common stock.
audit_findings.explanation: It is not demonstrated that none of the cash is excess, but the record also does not support treating all of it as distributable. The company expressly identifies working capital and acquisitions as uses of liquidity and relies on a floor-plan facility for daily operations. Because the bridge addition supplies roughly one-third of base equity value, even a moderate reserve is material.
audit_findings.action: Establish minimum operating cash from seasonal liquidity and cash-conversion-cycle data; identify restricted or committed balances, transaction and tax obligations, and sale proceeds already represented elsewhere; then rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Acquired-customer amortization may be stripped without a replacement-cost charge
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 purchased-intangible amortization was $20.625m pretax and $14.691m after its filed tax effect, with the after-tax amount equal to 23.1% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back customer-relationship amortization without deducting recurring acquisition or organic customer-replacement spending inflates maintainable OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Total amortization expense for purchased intangibles was $ 20.6 million, $ 19.9 million, and $ 15.2 million for the years ended March 31, 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates persistent purchased-intangible amortization of $20.625m, $19.929m, and $15.180m over FY2026-FY2024. It does not establish that amortization equals economic replacement cost, but acquisition cash outlays are outside the stated reinvestment deduction. The FY2026 after-tax add-back is large relative to the anchor and is reasonably capable of materially changing operating value.
audit_findings.action: Identify the exact amortization included in OE, attribute earnings to acquired customer relationships, estimate recurring acquisition and organic retention spending needed to maintain those earnings, and rerun OE with an evidence-supported replacement charge.

audit_findings.title: Divestiture-related other income and losses may remain in FY2026 OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.2m pretax contingent-consideration loss, approximately $3.0m after applying the filed 28.4% effective tax rate; transition-services earnings unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporary transition-services income overstates recurring OE, while retaining the contingent-consideration remeasurement loss understates it; both enter through FY2026 other income.
audit_findings.evidence: Our increase in other income was primarily due to higher interest income and lower foreign exchange losses in the current fiscal year period compared to the prior fiscal year and earnings from our transition services agreement with PEAC Solutions, offset by $4.2 million in expense in the current fiscal year related to adjustments to our estimate of the fair value of contingent consideration due from PEAC Solutions relating to our sale of HoldCo.
audit_findings.explanation: The $4.2m remeasurement loss is demonstrated, while the filing confirms transition-services earnings but does not quantify them. The valuation states that interest income was purged but provides no line-item reconciliation proving that these divestiture items were normalized. Their opposing effects are real, but the record cannot establish their net magnitude or materiality.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2026 other income line by line, quantify transition-services earnings, determine the tax effect of each divestiture item, remove both independently, and rerun FY2026 OE and the anchor if affected.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Reported FY2019 residual $6,516.0m, but its units are implicated by the demonstrated historical conversion error; valid magnitude unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A that is an eligible non-economic charge would be added back to historical OE and could increase the trend-derived anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2019 $6516.0m (35.0% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: Leaving unidentified D&A as an expense is conservative and therefore cannot overstate value. However, the residual's classification is unresolved, and its stated FY2019 amount cannot support a materiality conclusion while the same period contains demonstrated unit corruption. The valid potential uplift remains unquantified.
audit_findings.action: First repair FY2019 units and reconcile total filed D&A; then classify the residual by asset and economic character and rerun OE only for amounts supported as eligible add-backs.
